summary: On node1, added persistent fstab entries mounting /tmp and /dev/shm as tmpfs with noexec,nosuid,nodev, applied them live, verified enforcement (execution blocked on both), then performed the mandatory single-node restart: captured pre-restart boot_id and mount state, rebooted node1, polled until reachable, confirmed boot_id changed, and re-verified both mounts persisted with the correct options and still block execution after reboot.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 (RHEL 10.0): /tmp was part of root xfs (no separate mount); /dev/shm was tmpfs with nosuid,nodev but not noexec; no fstab entries existed for either
Backed up /etc/fstab and appended: tmpfs /tmp tmpfs defaults,nodev,nosuid,noexec 0 0 and tmpfs /dev/shm tmpfs defaults,nodev,nosuid,noexec 0 0
Ran systemctl daemon-reload, remounted /dev/shm with new options, mounted /tmp as tmpfs; detected and removed an accidental duplicate stacked mount on /tmp
Verified live: findmnt showed noexec,nosuid,nodev on both /tmp and /dev/shm; created+chmod+x'd test scripts on each and confirmed execution was denied (Permission denied, rc=126)
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id 434803ac-a01f-4272-ba59-a0cdb0c4dd92, both mounts healthy with correct options
Issued sudo systemctl reboot on node1; exec stream closed as expected
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again; confirmed new boot_id 52b2d6e3-ac2b-42a4-aec8-78a9f3af0dd1, proving an actual restart occurred
Post-restart verification: findmnt confirmed /tmp and /dev/shm still mounted with noexec,nosuid,nodev; re-ran exec tests on both, confirming execution remains blocked (rc=126) after reboot

evidence.requirement: Pre-change baseline state of /tmp and /dev/shm on node1
evidence.summary: Showed /tmp had no dedicated mount (part of root xfs) and /dev/shm was tmpfs missing noexec; no fstab entries present

evidence.requirement: Persistent config change: fstab entries for /tmp and /dev/shm with noexec,nosuid,nodev
evidence.summary: cat /etc/fstab shows new tmpfs lines for /tmp and /dev/shm with defaults,nodev,nosuid,noexec after backing up the original file

evidence.requirement: Live activation of the new mount options
evidence.summary: daemon-reload, remount of /dev/shm, mount of /tmp all succeeded; detected and cleaned a duplicate stacked /tmp mount leaving one clean mount

evidence.requirement: Functional proof that noexec/nosuid/nodev are enforced pre-reboot
evidence.summary: findmnt confirms options on both mounts; executing chmod+x scripts placed in /tmp and /dev/shm both fail with Permission denied (rc=126)

evidence.requirement: node1 healthy baseline and boot identity before restart
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 434803ac-a01f-4272-ba59-a0cdb0c4dd92 and confirmed /tmp and /dev/shm mounts healthy with correct options prior to reboot
systemctl reboot issued; exec stream closed before completion, consistent with the node going down for restart

evidence.requirement: node1 changed boot identity confirming actual restart
evidence.summary: After polling through connection timeouts, exec succeeded again with new boot_id 52b2d6e3-ac2b-42a4-aec8-78a9f3af0dd1, differing from the pre-restart boot_id, proving a real reboot occurred

evidence.requirement: node1 recovered state: mount hardening persisted across reboot
evidence.summary: Post-reboot findmnt shows /tmp and /dev/shm both still mounted with noexec,nosuid,nodev, and functional test scripts on each again fail to execute (rc=126), proving the hardening survived the restart
